`tax_for()` in `src/billing/tax.py` now rounds half-up. It was actually unimplemented before (it just raised `NotImplementedError`), so this is a new implementation, not a change to existing rounding:

```python
tax = Decimal(amount_cents) * Decimal(str(rate))
return int(tax.quantize(Decimal(1), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))
```

It rounds to whole cents. I convert `rate` through `str` so a rate passed as a float, like `0.0825`, doesn't pick up float error.

I checked it by calling it directly: 250 × 0.05 gives 13 (half-even would have given 12), and 350 × 0.05 gives 18. I couldn't run the test suite because pytest isn't installed here. There are also no existing tests for `tax_for`; `tests/test_tax.py` only covers `line_total`.

**Memory update:** The project memory still recorded the March 2026 decision to use banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`) and said not to use half-up. I saved a new memory that replaces it: tax rounds half-up, per your note that finance reversed the decision. That way future sessions won't "fix" this back.
